dial.summary: TOTAL crypto recovered 0.3% to $2.98T on September 26 as Strait of Hormuz deal hopes boosted risk sentiment, with BTC.D easing slightly to 56.5% on mild altcoin outperformance; DXY slipped to ~100.99 (still a headwind above 100) while real yields hold at 2.81% — yet global M2 holds its 4-week uptrend at $103.4T, near-zero BTC funding (0.0095%) confirms unlevered positioning, and the 2s10s curve bounced to +0.36%, sustaining the BTC Accumulation posture ahead of the Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at $103,372B ($103.4T) as of September 24, 2026 per MacroMicro (6–8 week reporting lag); US M2 at $23.3T in August 2026 per MacroRadar (+5.4% YoY trajectory); 4-week trend up: ~$103.0T (Aug 26) → $103.4T (Sep 24) = +0.4% over 4 weeks, meeting the supportive threshold; status supportive (4-week rising trend confirmed); no new G4 aggregate print expected until early October given the reporting lag; Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP are next major macro catalysts that could affect the forward M2 outlook.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1); September ISM Manufacturing releases October 1 — no new official ISM reading as of September 26; LEADING SIGNAL: S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI for September surged to 57.0 (52-month high, released Sep 23) and composite hit 58.4 (62-month high), pointing to potential ISM upside on Oct 1; 4-week trend down: July 55.6% (ISM value ~30 days before the Aug 54.6% release) → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (ISM above 50 but falling on 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 or above 62 — neither applies); a Sep ISM print above 55 and rising would shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at ~100.99 on September 26, 2026 (down 0.06% from Sep 25 close of 101.0555, pressured by Strait of Hormuz deal hopes boosting risk sentiment); 4-week trend up: ~99.60 (Aug 26 per Barchart) → 100.99 (Sep 26) = +1.4% over 4 weeks, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold (barely, at 100.99); hawkish Fed stance (fed funds 3.75%–4.00% post Sep 16 hike) and elevated real yields (2.81%) underpin USD strength; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status; the marginal DXY decline today keeps both DXY and real yields as the two active macro headwinds; trend derivation consistent with 30-day DTWEXBGS broad dollar index movement.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.81% as of September 24, 2026 (latest available; FRED does not publish on weekends — Sep 26 is Saturday); breakeven inflation rate near 2.27%; 10Y nominal near 5.11%; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 22) → 2.81% (Sep 24) = +36bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met, with margin); next DFII10 observation expected Monday Sep 29; Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP are next catalysts for potential repricing; a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral/supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 26, 2026: 2s10s spread bounced to +0.36% (+36bps) from its flattest reading of the year, per 247 Wall St; curve widened 5bps from Sep 24 close of +0.31%; 4-week trend flat: ~+38bps (Aug 26, pre-FOMC range) → +36bps (Sep 26) = −2bps over 4 weeks, well within the <5bps flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening on 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); the bounce off the year's flattest reading is constructive but insufficient to confirm a sustained steepening trend; October 27–28 FOMC is the next major repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,748B ($6.748T) for week ending September 23, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 24 (Treasuries $4,558B, MBS $1,910B, other $279B); no new H.4.1 release on Saturday Sep 26; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.734T (Aug 26, estimated from weekly progression) → $6.748T (Sep 23) = +$14B over ~4 weeks, marginal expansion within flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity); total assets up ~$138B year-on-year; Fed balance sheet remains non-inflationary at current trajectory.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.0095% per 8h as of September 22, 2026 (latest available per MacroMicro); total crypto market recovered 0.3% to $2.98T on September 26, with BTC.D easing to 56.5% ($1.68T BTC market cap) as altcoins modestly outperformed; in a mild risk-on recovery environment with real yields at 2.81%, funding rates near zero confirm the bounce is spot-driven and unlevered; 30-day range has been consistently sub-0.01% throughout September; status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP are next potential catalysts for a funding regime change.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$309B (USDT ~$183B/60.6% of stablecoins, USDC ~$74B); total crypto market cap $2.98T (TOTAL per CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap, up 0.3% on the day); stablecoin dominance 10.4% ($309B / $2.98T); 30-day trend down: dominance peaked at ~13% in Q1 2026 and trended down through September from ~10.5–11.0% (Aug 26) to 10.4% (Sep 26) — the denominator (TOTAL) rising while stablecoin supply is flat drives the decline; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply since TOTAL is rising today and dominance is flat/declining); BTC.D 56.5% on Sep 26, down from 57.29% (Sep 25) as TOTAL recovered.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster (Fed +25bps Sep 16, BOJ +25bps Sep 18); DXY eased to ~100.99 and TOTAL crypto recovered 0.3% to $2.98T on Sep 26, but real yields remain at 2.81% and the 10Y nominal near 5.11%; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs are weighing on consumer psychology; August PCE and Q2 GDP third estimate follow the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside August PCE (Sep 30), September NFP (Oct 2), and FOMC Minutes (Oct 7).

upcoming.title: Q2 2026 GDP (Third Estimate)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis Q2 2026 GDP third (final) estimate at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside August PCE and ADP; a downward revision would add to recession concerns given the FOMC's hawkish Sep 16 hike and real yields at 2.81%; a strong final print would confirm the economy can absorb the current rate cycle, consistent with S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) on September 23; includes BEA annual updates of national, industry, and regional data.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays report including August 2026 PCE Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; July 2026 PCE was +3.7% YoY; a reading above +3.5% YoY reinforces the FOMC's case for continued tightening ahead of October 27–28; core PCE (ex food and energy) watched most closely; released alongside Q2 GDP third estimate and ADP; the last major inflation print before the October FOMC blackout period begins.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP Research Institute private payrolls estimate for September 2026 at 8:15 AM ET — advance read on labor conditions ahead of official NFP (Oct 2); released alongside Q2 GDP and August PCE on a data-dense final day of September; a strong print (+150K or above) reinforces the NFP-resilient narrative and keeps rate-hike expectations elevated for the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — most consequential ISM read in months; August ISM was 54.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI surged to 57.0 (52-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal; an ISM print above 55 and rising would shift the ISM indicator to supportive status and likely push DXY higher and real yields further up; a move below 50 would signal contraction and support a shift toward Risk Off posture.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 26, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 26, 2026 — released same day as ISM Manufacturing PMI; a back-to-back rise in claims would be an early signal that cumulative rate tightening (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) is beginning to bite on employment; prior weeks approximately 206K.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation — September 2026 NFP
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (first Friday of October) — the most consequential pre-FOMC data release before the October 27–28 meeting; August NFP was +162K; a reading above +200K with unemployment holding sub-4.5% keeps October hike odds elevated; a surprise miss below +100K could shift the rate path significantly; watch average hourly earnings for wage inflation signals; released 25 days before the next FOMC decision.
